items.definition:
recoil in embarrassment or disgust
I always cringe when I watch old videos of myself.

to allow oneself to enjoy the pleasure of something
I decided to indulge in a piece of chocolate cake.

to kill in a violent way; to impress greatly
The knight went forth to slay the dragon.

to move goods illegally into or out of a country
They tried to smuggle drugs across the border.

to join metal parts by heating
He learned how to weld metal in his workshop.

to fight in a rough or noisy way
Two men started to brawl outside the bar.

to comply with rules, standards, or laws
Students are expected to conform to the school rules.

to grow or develop in a healthy or vigorous way
The business began to flourish after the new marketing campaign.

to set someone or something free from a situation
The army fought to liberate the occupied city.

to be or remain hidden so as to wait in ambush
A danger might lurk around the corner.

to move skillfully or carefully
The pilot had to maneuver the plane through the storm.

to leave out or exclude
Please omit any unnecessary details from your report.

to make something unique to a particular person
You can personalize your phone with a custom ringtone.

to cut or gather a crop; to receive a reward or consequence
You reap what you sow.

to compensate for faults or shortcomings; to save from sin
He tried to redeem himself after making a mistake.

to cut off (a part of a whole) or cut through
The rope was severed by the sharp rock.

grab quickly
He tried to snatch the bag from her hand.

broadcast on television
The event will be televised live around the world.

to hold dear; to feel or show great love for
I will always cherish the memories of our time together.

to think deeply about something
He sat quietly, contemplating his next move.

to completely destroy a building
The old factory was demolished to make way for new apartments.

to cut or carve a text or design on a hard surface
They decided to engrave their names on the back of the watch.

to create or devise
They need to formulate a new plan.

to live in
Many species inhabit this forest.

to have too high an opinion of
I think people tend to overrate that movie; it wasn't that great.

to create again or anew
They tried to recreate the original recipe, but it wasn't quite the same.

to make someone aware of or familiar with
Please allow me to acquaint you with the new procedures.

Work jointly on an activity or project.
They decided to collaborate on the research project.

Make an unjust or prejudicial distinction in the treatment of different categories of people or things; perceive or recognize the difference between.
It is illegal to discriminate against someone based on their age.

to intervene between people in a dispute in order to bring about an agreement or reconciliation
The lawyer tried to mediate the dispute between the two parties.

to supervise a person or their work, especially in an official capacity
She was hired to oversee the entire project.

to stimulate or incite (someone) to do or feel something, especially by arousing anger in them
His rude comments were meant to provoke a reaction.

print again
The publisher decided to reprint the popular novel.

to put or go underwater
The submarine can submerge to great depths.

be next to and joined with
The two properties adjoin each other.

feel contempt or a deep repugnance for
She despises people who are dishonest.

scatter or spread over a wide area
The police used tear gas to disperse the crowd.

begin a course of action, especially one that is important or demanding
They decided to embark on a new business venture.

improve or enhance the quality or value of
Reading can greatly enrich your vocabulary.

to light up; to make clear
The streetlights illuminate the path at night.

walk unsteadily
He began to stagger after drinking too much.

hold on tightly
The child would cling to his mother's hand.

happen at the same time
Their holidays happened to coincide.

change direction
The police had to divert traffic.

inform or instruct
Please enlighten me on this topic.

To imitate, especially in order to entertain or ridicule.
The comedian could mimic various accents perfectly.

To tip over; to reverse a decision.
The boat might overturn in the strong waves.

officially cancel or withdraw
The company decided to revoke his license.

imitate the appearance or character of
Pilots train in a simulator to simulate real flight conditions.

to take or seize (someone's property) with authority
The police had to confiscate the illegal goods.

to discourage (someone) from doing something by instilling doubt or fear
The high fences were meant to deter intruders.

drive, push, or cause to move in a particular direction
The engine propels the boat through the water.

prevent (someone or something) from doing something; keep under control or check
He had to restrain himself from laughing.

form a theory or conjecture about a subject without firm evidence
We can only speculate about what happened.

refrain from insisting on or using (a right or claim)
They decided to waive the late fee for us.

make (a problem, injury, or offense) worse or more serious
Don't scratch that mosquito bite, you'll only aggravate it.

concentrate (control or power) in a central organization
The company decided to centralize its operations in one office.

publicly declare to be wrong or evil
The government was quick to denounce the terrorist attack.

make (a liquid) thinner or weaker by adding water or another solvent to it
You should dilute the juice with water before drinking it.

make or become more intense or severe
The tension in the room began to heighten as the deadline approached.

to reconsider (something), especially in a fundamental way
We need to rethink our strategy for the project.

to show approval by clapping
The audience began to applaud loudly.

to perform a baptism
The priest will baptize the baby next Sunday.

to praise excessively or insincerely
He tried to flatter his boss to get a raise.
